conclusion: 18 req/s passed the short complete-cohort success/TPOT gates, but MUSA queues grew; long-term stable capacity was not validated. The 1/3 vendor-pool split feeds MUSA about 6 req/s while it completes about 5.17 req/s at a nearly full 7x16 running budget.
queue_mechanism: At 18 req/s Gateway waiting was zero; MUSA model waiting mean 120.91 and peak 252, first-third mean 44.28 and last-third mean 202.63. Pool-local queues are balanced; inter-pool allocation and MUSA service capacity are the main factors to investigate.
limits: TPOT is the per-request average after first content; it excludes queue/prefill/first-token delay.
MUSA eager versus Ascend/Iluvatar graphs; no same-mode hardware ranking.
.23 SMI missing: Ascend utilization has 16/26 device coverage.
Synthetic repeated workload, one run per point, no long-duration validation or semantic scoring.
No causal A/B run of pool weights or max_num_seqs was performed.

historical_16_interpretation: 16 req/s was tested three times with 29 workers. All 4800-request cohorts were 100% successful. One cache_aware stage also passed the original queue gate with 99.9167% SLO attainment; a later cache_aware stage had 100% SLO attainment but failed the original queue gate (.96 +3.15, .97 +3.85). These valid historical results must be reported, but are not an identical-configuration lower point for the current 28-worker experiment. Only their saved stage summaries are available locally; historical per-request logs were not recomputed.
